title: The Crunch, Passed Through

source.title: How Airlines Actually Hedge Higher Fuel Prices

lines.quote: every time oil jumps: 'did they hedge their fuel?' — and the conversation stops there; we all talk about it and have no idea what it means
lines.note: names the shadow at the door: the hedge as the story, the crunch underneath it unasked
lines.zWhy: no claim on the crunch; a claim about the word

lines.quote: fuel is the second biggest cost after labor, and the most volatile
lines.note: sizes the exposure
lines.zWhy: volatility is the price's register, not a dent

lines.quote: there's always another lever: raise fares, raise the fuel surcharge — when shortages are in the news, customers aren't going to complain
lines.note: THE PASS-THROUGH, stated: the crunch becomes a line on the ticket, and the news is the licence to print it

lines.quote: airline prices are very expensive; bookings are really high too — new TSA records, new global records; we are flying a lot
lines.note: dates the activity (as-of 09-29): no dent

lines.quote: recording this September 29th; back in February or March when the Iran war broke out we were all staring at the Singapore jet fuel chart
lines.note: dates the window: the war's onset and the first chart; the tape's as-of
lines.zWhy: a date, not a reading of the bite

lines.quote: with oil prices spiking again with the shortage of diesel, this has suddenly become a very relevant topic
lines.note: registers the diesel crunch as the occasion — the object named once, then left for the mechanism
lines.zWhy: 'relevant' prices it as a topic, not a shortage

lines.quote: the US carriers got smacked in 2014–15; Delta lost over a billion in 2020; the smaller airlines put everything into the surcharge — we pass all the cost on to the customer, built into the ticket
lines.note: the mechanism, dated: the US fleet is structurally pass-through; the hedge book was the casualty of the last two cycles

lines.quote: think of an airline like a refinery: the refinery sells the crack; the airline is short fuel to fly the plane and long fuel through the ticket
lines.note: THE MODEL. The lowest-Dia line in the tape — not one adjective
lines.zWhy: the model is built on pass-through holding

lines.quote: you use Brent as your proxy because the jet market is too thin; the American carriers use heating oil
lines.note: names the instrument and its basis: the hedge is on the wrong molecule by necessity
lines.zWhy: no claim on the crunch

lines.quote: some airlines are too cheap to pay for their calls, so they fund it by selling puts — the zero-cost collar
lines.note: the plain vanilla; 'too cheap' is the one vehicle word
lines.zWhy: no claim on the crunch

lines.quote: what I structured at JP Morgan was a target redemption note — vanilla on one side, exotic on the other; I sold both wings: calls above 120, puts below 80
lines.note: the exotic, dated (2006–); the strangle that reappears at 33:22
lines.zWhy: no claim on the crunch

lines.quote: heating oil versus WTI went through $100 for the crack — $107; 230 bucks a barrel while crude trades at 110; Brent nearly 120; a 74–75 dollar gas-oil crack in Europe
lines.note: SIZES THE CRUNCH as-of 09-29: the product crack at a record. The shortage, in the price's own units

lines.quote: there's no real open market for jet in Europe; Argus or Platts print a number with no offer behind it, or no bid — they just pick a number; very arbitrary
lines.note: the price itself is thin: an assessed number, not a trade. The method reaches the object and finds there isn't one
lines.zWhy: a claim about the measurement, not the bite

lines.quote: normalized to early February: Brent rose 50%; Singapore jet more than doubled — a well-hedged carrier hedging Brent still bleeding
lines.note: the basis break, dated by the terminal: the hedge misses the product

lines.quote: Singapore jet is a different animal: certain trading houses with certain oil majors control that market; the only buyers are airlines; how would I put this nicely — sometimes people talk to each other. Not an objective market
lines.note: →PG01: who sets the number. The market as a room; the incumbents' price. Spoken as an aside, with the disclaimer the fluid register makes before it says something
lines.zWhy: a controlled price is a price that bites the buyer

lines.quote: hedging helps when oil is low — the surcharge can't do anything then, and when oil is low the economy isn't: 1998, 2008, 2020, and right now with the 2026 war between Iran and the US and Israel
lines.note: dates the pattern and places 2026 in the series
lines.zWhy: the series is one of price cycles passed through

lines.quote: the surcharge doesn't go through P&L but the hedge does; done well you make twice as much money; right now the surcharge is probably 25% of the ticket
lines.note: the pass-through sized: a quarter of the ticket is the crunch, and it is invisible in the accounts

lines.quote: 44% — nearly half our expenses was jet fuel
lines.note: sizes Qatar's exposure (2011–13)
lines.zWhy: a 2011 number; no claim on 2026

lines.quote: when oil comes down we lose on the hedge book and on revenue: the economy isn't hot, the plane doesn't take off — a double whammy; 'I do not want to see red anymore'
lines.note: the precedent (2011–12) and the mandate; the story-telling register at its most fluid
lines.zWhy: the precedent is of pass-through failing from the other side

lines.quote: we ran correlations between the fuel surcharge and Brent: 75%; our Brent swap was 85–88% correlated with jet — so the airline is long oil through the ticket; even revenue management didn't know they were long oil
lines.note: THE FINDING: the pass-through measured. The line the whole episode exists to carry

lines.quote: the word hedging is a misnomer — it's a view, it's a trade; compliance goes ballistic, so they say no, we're not trading, we're hedging
lines.note: names the shadow from inside: 'hedging' as a word that hides a view. The 2:14 line answered
lines.zWhy: no claim on the crunch

lines.quote: $130 million; revenue lost 65 that year; the hedge let revenue management cut fares 20% — first-mover; every plane 80–90% full
lines.note: the result, dated (2012): the ticket-funded view paid for fares

lines.quote: Qatar Petroleum sold us jet at $3.65 a gallon; Chevron in Dubai at $2.95 — screwed 70% by our own national petroleum company; the 787 'training flights' flew to Dubai on fumes and lifted 100 tons
lines.note: →PG01: the national oil company as a counterparty, priced; the tankering anecdote. 'Screwed' is the vehicle
lines.zWhy: 2011–13; no claim on 2026

lines.quote: they're very wary of consumption hedging, mainly passing it through to the customer because they don't know what to do; a highly ranked Asian airline lost nearly two billion in 2020; use your ticket as your weapon of choice
lines.note: THE READING OF NOW (09-29): the industry's answer to the crunch is the ticket. 'Weapon' is the one vehicle word

lines.quote: we have this diesel crisis in the United States; diesel prices are surging; it's possible the US implements a ban on diesel exports — when you hear this, what do you think about?
lines.note: puts the register's object on the table, as a question
lines.zWhy: a question

lines.quote: maybe it's not right for me to say this, but I think of TACO — Trump
lines.note: the one denominated line in the tape: the ban read as character, by acronym; the disclaimer first. Compare Krystal 5:52 (the same gap read as an instrument)
lines.zWhy: 'always chickens out': the ban won't happen; rhetoric, not a bite

lines.quote: Russia's done that; Russia is the second biggest diesel exporter on the planet — a lot of diesel has been taken out of the whole complex; Europe is pretty short; London gas oil through the roof
lines.note: →PG01 (Russian theater): the physical side, dated. Supply removed; Europe short

lines.quote: this export ban, a lot of it was rhetoric — because of that rhetoric, heating oil in the US came down instead of up
lines.note: the rhetoric priced: the threat moved the number the other way. The jawbone read from the RI side — the instrument, not the man

lines.quote: PADD 3 is the kitchen; the East Coast buys diesel from Europe, a seaborne trade; most heating oil goes to Latin America; a Gulf-to-Asia trade through the Canal
lines.note: the plumbing, dated: where the barrels go and why the ban would move the wrong number
lines.zWhy: the plumbing routes around a ban

lines.quote: can't wait to heat my house in Connecticut this winter
lines.note: the crunch brought home as a joke — the only first-person line, and the only one that expects to feel it
lines.zWhy: the joke expects the bite

lines.quote: you don't have to take a directional view if you understand the structural position of the company — an airline is of course short oil, and in certain environments implicitly long oil
lines.note: the takeaway, restated: the pass-through is the position
lines.zWhy: 'implicitly long' is pass-through holding

lines.quote: there's a lot of elasticity baked into airfares in a big oil shock; but if we evolve into actual physical shortages, which is a possibility — we'll see
lines.note: STATES THE FALSIFIER: physical shortage is the test of pass-through. The one line in the tape with the Z-axis spoken out loud

lines.quote: the airline industry encapsulates the economy right now: the cost of everything is going up and people are flying like crazy; it has not dented activity at all. This is a hot economy
lines.note: the reading, concluded: it passes through; no dent. The segment's z, stated as a fact about the economy
